kingdom-of-great-zimbabwe.name: Kingdom of Great Zimbabwe
kingdom-of-great-zimbabwe.summary: A Shona kingdom whose capital, Great Zimbabwe, was the largest stone structure in precolonial Southern Africa, dominating regional gold trade from around 1300 before its unexplained decline after the 15th century.

shona-people.name: Shona people
shona-people.summary: A Bantu ethnic group native to Southern Africa forming the majority in Zimbabwe, who migrated from the Congo River basin around the end of the first millennium and built a great civilization there.

great-zimbabwe.name: Great Zimbabwe
great-zimbabwe.summary: A city in south-eastern Zimbabwe settled around 1000 AD, capital of the Kingdom of Great Zimbabwe from the 13th century and the largest stone structure in precolonial Southern Africa, built by ancestors of the Shona people.

kingdom-of-kongo.name: Kingdom of Kongo
kingdom-of-kongo.summary: A Central African kingdom spanning parts of modern Angola, Congo and Gabon, independent from around 1390 to 1862, later a Portuguese vassal until its monarchy was abolished in 1914.

kingdom-of-mapungubwe.name: Kingdom of Mapungubwe
kingdom-of-mapungubwe.summary: An ancient southern African state at the Shashe-Limpopo confluence, with a capital of 5,000 people by 1250, that traded gold and ivory via the Indian Ocean before declining around 1300.

luanda.name: Luanda
luanda.summary: Capital and largest city of Angola, founded by the Portuguese in 1576, which served as a center of the slave trade to Brazil before it was prohibited.

benguela.name: Benguela
benguela.summary: A city in western Angola and capital of Benguela Province, one of the country's most populous cities.

zimbabwe-bird.name: Zimbabwe Bird
zimbabwe-bird.summary: A soapstone national emblem of Zimbabwe, based on carvings found at the ruins of Great Zimbabwe, likely representing a sacred eagle in Shona tradition.

masvingo.name: Masvingo
masvingo.summary: A city in southeastern Zimbabwe, formerly Fort Victoria, located near the Great Zimbabwe ruins and populated mostly by the Karanga people.

khami.name: Khami
khami.summary: A ruined city near Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, once capital of the Kingdom of Butua under the Torwa dynasty. It is now a national monument and UNESCO World Heritage Site.

danamombe.name: Danamombe
danamombe.summary: A Zimbabwean archaeological site near Gweru whose stone ruins resemble those of Khami, close to the smaller Naletale ruins.

naletale.name: Naletale
naletale.summary: Stone ruins in Zimbabwe attributed to the Kalanga Torwa State, dating from the seventeenth century and later used under Rozvi rule; declared a national monument in 1960.

mwari.name: Mwari
mwari.summary: The supreme creator deity in Shona and Venda traditional religion, believed to be the author of all things and all life, worshipped mainly in Mozambique, South Africa and Zimbabwe.

african-fish-eagle.name: African fish eagle (hungwe)
african-fish-eagle.summary: A large fish-eating eagle found across sub-Saharan Africa, called hungwe in Shona, and the national bird of Malawi, Namibia, Zambia and Zimbabwe.

manilla-money.name: Manillas
manilla-money.summary: Brass, bronze or copper rings used as commodity money in West Africa from before the colonial period until the late 1940s, closely associated with the Atlantic slave trade.

afonso-i-of-kongo.name: Afonso I of Kongo
afonso-i-of-kongo.summary: Sixth ruler of the Kingdom of Kongo, reigning from 1509 to 1542 or 1543; a devout Catholic convert who centralized royal power, expanded the kingdom through war, and deepened ties with Portugal.

nsundi.name: Nsundi
nsundi.summary: A former province of the Kingdom of Kongo, with its capital near the Inkisi River in what is now the Democratic Republic of Congo.

m-banza-kongo.name: Mbanza Kongo
m-banza-kongo.summary: Capital of the Kingdom of Kongo from before Portuguese contact in 1483 until 1915; now a city in Angola and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2017.

tio-kingdom.name: Tio Kingdom
tio-kingdom.summary: A West Central African kingdom founded around the 14th century in what is now the Republic of the Congo and DR Congo, a longtime rival of the Kingdom of Kongo.

jo-o-i-of-kongo.name: João I of Kongo
jo-o-i-of-kongo.summary: João I of Kongo: Fifth ruler of the Kingdom of Kongo (1470–1509), born Nzinga-a-Nkuwu; he converted to Catholicism after Portuguese sailors arrived, taking the name João, but abandoned the faith in 1495, partly over its requirement of monogamy.

manikongo.name: Manikongo
manikongo.summary: The title of the ruler of the Kingdom of Kongo (14th–19th centuries), who appointed provincial governors and received tribute, ruling from the capital Mbanza Kongo.

nyatsimba-mutota.name: Nyatsimba Mutota
nyatsimba-mutota.summary: A member of Great Zimbabwe's royal family, active around 1400–1450, credited as the first king of the Mutapa Empire, which his son's conquests later extended to the Indian Ocean.

guruuswa.name: Guruuswa
guruuswa.summary: Historical region in modern-day Zimbabwe whose name means "long grass" in Shona. Shona oral traditions hold that their people originated there.

teve-kingdom.name: Teve kingdom
teve-kingdom.summary: Precolonial state in modern Mozambique, ruled by a Sachiteve. It broke away from Mutapa in the early 16th century and sought to control the trade route from Portuguese-held Sofala to the gold-producing Manyika region.

manyika-people.name: Manyika people
manyika-people.summary: Shona sub-group that originated from the Manyika kingdom, living mainly in eastern Zimbabwe and western Mozambique and speaking several dialects.

james-the-great.name: James the Great
james-the-great.summary: One of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus, who died around AD 44 and was the first apostle to be martyred. He is the patron saint of Spain, and tradition holds his remains lie in Santiago de Compostela.

kalala-ilunga.name: Kalala Ilunga
kalala-ilunga.summary: Mythic hero and first sacred king of the Luba Kingdom, remembered as its most revered son and credited with inventing much of Luba culture. He is said to be from the 16th century.

catholic-church-in-kongo.name: Kala ka Mfusu
catholic-church-in-kongo.summary: Kongo nobleman kidnapped by the Portuguese in 1483 and taken to Portugal, where he converted to Christianity; he later led a royal mission to Portugal, dying on the return voyage in 1491.

ambundu.name: Ambundu
ambundu.summary: A Bantu people on a plateau in present-day Angola, speaking Kimbundu and forming about a quarter of Angola's population.

kongo-people.name: Kongo people
kongo-people.summary: A Bantu ethnic group and speakers of Kikongo who lived along the Atlantic coast in the kingdoms of Kongo, Loango and Kakongo, and were among the first Africans to meet Portuguese traders in 1483.

jan-vansina.name: Jan Vansina
jan-vansina.summary: Belgian historian and anthropologist (1929–2017) regarded as a leading authority on Central African history and a pioneer of using oral tradition as historical evidence.

kongo-language.name: Kikongo
kongo-language.summary: A Bantu language of the Kongo people spoken by around seven million people in Central Africa, historically carried across the Atlantic by enslaved Africans.

pende-people.name: Pende
pende-people.summary: An ethnic group of over 250,000 people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, known for their distinctive art and divided into Eastern and Western cultural branches.

diogo-c-o.name: Diogo Cão
diogo-c-o.summary: Portuguese mariner and explorer (c. 1452–1486) who made two voyages along the west coast of Africa in the 1480s, exploring the Congo River and the coasts of Angola and Namibia.

padr-o.name: Padrão
padr-o.summary: A stone pillar left by Portuguese explorers in the 15th and 16th centuries to mark landfalls and claim territory.

cape-cross.name: Cape Cross
cape-cross.summary: A headland on the Skeleton Coast of western Namibia, on the South Atlantic coast.

pool-malebo.name: Pool Malebo
pool-malebo.summary: A broad, lake-like widening of the lower Congo River forming the border between Brazzaville and Kinshasa; long a key cultural, commercial and political hub for local peoples.

mbata-kingdom.name: Mbata Kingdom
mbata-kingdom.summary: A Bantu kingdom north of Mpemba Kasi that merged with it around 1375 to help form the Kingdom of Kongo, following a political marriage between the two peoples' rulers.

swahili-coast.name: Swahili coast
swahili-coast.summary: An East African coastal region inhabited by the Swahili people, whose trading towns blended African and Arab culture and were described by writers such as Ibn Battuta.

mutapa-empire.name: Mutapa Empire
mutapa-empire.summary: A Shona empire on the northern Zimbabwean Plateau, also called Mwenemutapa or Monomotapa, whose ruler's title meant 'Lord of the Conquered Land' and came to name the whole kingdom.

lukeni-lua-nimi.name: Lukeni lua Nimi
lukeni-lua-nimi.summary: Traditional founder of the Kongo dynasty and first king of the Kingdom of Kongo, reigning around 1380 to 1420 after conquering the kingdom of Mwene.

ingombe-ilede.name: Ingombe Ilede
ingombe-ilede.summary: An archaeological site in Zambia near the Zambezi River, a major 16th-century trading centre for salt, copper, gold, ivory and slaves linked to Indian Ocean trade goods.

kingdom-of-butua.name: Kingdom of Butua
kingdom-of-butua.summary: A Kalanga kingdom in what is now southwestern Zimbabwe from about 1425 to 1683, known as a source of gold for Arab and Portuguese traders until its conquest by Changamire Dombo.

nzambi-ampungu.name: Nzambi Ampungu
nzambi-ampungu.summary: The Supreme God and eternal Sky Father of traditional Kongo spirituality, associated with the sun; his female counterpart rules the moon. After Portuguese colonization he became identified with the Christian God.

kongo-religion.name: Kongo religion
kongo-religion.summary: The traditional animistic beliefs of the Bakongo people, centered on the creator god Nzambi Ampungu and on ancestor veneration.

nganga.name: Nganga
nganga.summary: A spiritual healer, diviner and ritual specialist in traditional Kongo religion, also found among descendants of Kongo and Mbundu peoples across the African diaspora, including Brazil, Cuba and Haiti.

molefi-kete-asante.name: Molefi Kete Asante
molefi-kete-asante.summary: American philosopher and professor at Temple University who advocates Afrocentricity, founded its PhD program in African-American Studies, and has written more than 90 books.

kongo-cosmogram.name: Dikenga (Kongo cosmogram)
kongo-cosmogram.summary: A core symbol of Kongo religion showing the physical and spiritual worlds, the sun's rotation, and the four stages of life, drawn as a cross within a circle.

chokwe-people.name: Chokwe
chokwe-people.summary: A Bantu ethnic group of Central and Southern Africa, found mainly in Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Zambia, known for varied traditional artwork.

john-thornton-historian.name: John Thornton
john-thornton-historian.summary: American historian (born 1949) at Boston University specializing in African, African Diaspora and Atlantic World history.

linda-heywood.name: Linda Heywood
linda-heywood.summary: Caribbean-American historian specializing in African, especially Angolan, history; co-author with her husband John Thornton of award-winning work on Central Africans and the Atlantic world.

sofala.name: Sofala
sofala.summary: A historic Swahili city-state on the coast of Mozambique, first used as a port by Mogadishan merchants and known as a hub of the gold trade.

kilwa-sultanate.name: Kilwa Sultanate
kilwa-sultanate.summary: A sultanate centered on the island of Kilwa off Tanzania, whose authority at its height stretched along the whole Swahili Coast; legend credits its founding to a Persian prince in the 10th century.

lefini-river.name: Lefini River
lefini-river.summary: A river in the Republic of Congo and tributary of the Congo River, reached by explorer Henry Morton Stanley on 9 March 1877.

john-ii-of-portugal.name: John II of Portugal
john-ii-of-portugal.summary: King of Portugal from 1481 to 1495, known as the Perfect Prince, who restored royal power, revived the economy and renewed Portuguese exploration of Africa and Asia.

kingdom-of-loango.name: Kingdom of Loango
kingdom-of-loango.summary: A Kongo-founded state on Africa's Atlantic coast from roughly the 1500s to 1800s, exporting copper and cloth, at its height reaching from Cape St Catherine near the Congo River's mouth.
